title.narrative: National Urban Cadaster and Municipal Support Project

description.narrative: The development objective of National Urban Cadaster and Municipal Support Project for Peru is to improve the coverage of urban cadaster services in selected municipalities to enhance local government capacities for revenue generation and urban management. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Strengthening municipal systems, services and capacities to generate and maintain urban cadasters in project municipalities, has the following two sub components: (a) Creation of an urban cadastral information system for tax purposes and urban management in selected municipalities; and (b) Strengthening municipal capacity. 2) The second component, Strengthening of the national institutional framework, aims to finance the activities to be conducted at the national level. 3) The third component, Project management, aims to finance the establishment and staffing of a project implementation unit (PIU) within informal agency (COFOPRI), which will be responsible for procurement, FM, social and environmental safeguards activities, and monitoring the results of the project.
The project development objective is to improve the coverage of urban cadaster services in selected municipalities to enhance local government capacities for revenue generation and urban management.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I A2 (a). To facilitate the implementation of the Project the Borrower, through MVCS, shall by no later thanninety (90) days after Effective Date create and maintain, throughout Project implementation a steering committee (the SteeringCommittee) led by MVCS, responsible for strategic direction, project oversight and coordination with stakeholders, approval of mainProject operational instruments and selection of key personnel of PIU, and with composition and functions set forth in theOperations Manual.

Schedule 2, Section I A2 (b). To facilitate the implementation of the Project the Borrower shall by no later than thirty (30) daysafter Effective Date, create and maintain, throughout Project implementation, a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within COFOPRI,with functions, staffing, and responsibilities satisfactory to the Bank, as set forth in the Operations Manual.

Schedule 2, Section I B. Prior to the carrying out of any Project activity under the jurisdiction of a Selected Municipality, theBorrower, through MVCS and COFOPRI, shall enter into a Cooperation Agreement with every Selected Municipality, under terms andconditions acceptable to the Bank.

Schedule 2, Section I C1. The Borrower, through COFOPRI, shall carry out the Project in accordance with the provisions of a manual(the Operations Manual), satisfactory to the Bank, containing, inter alia: (a) the activities and timetable of actions to becarriedout under the Project; (b) the composition and responsibilities of the PIU and Steering Committee; (c) the fiduciary,technical and operational aspects and procedures for implementation of the Project, including the financial management procedures(budgeting, accounting and internal control, disbursement and flow of funds, financial reporting, annual reports, internal andexternal audit arrangements procedures); and (d) the performance indicators for the Project.

Schedule 2, Section I C2. The Borrower, through COFOPRI, shall not amend or waive or fail to enforce any provision of theOperations Manual without the Bank's prior written approval. In case of any conflict between the terms of the Operations Manual andthose of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall prevail.

title.narrative: Percentage of plots registered by the Project that are linked to land use and zoning data

comment.narrative: As of December 2025, 647,993 cadastral units have been surveyed across Areas 1 and 2, of which 113,852 units have successfully passed all quality control stages (from Area 1). The contract for Area 2 expired on May 12, 2025, and the service provider (Seresco) has not resolved persistent quality inconsistencies, which is leading toward contract termination. Consequently, the Implementing Agency has prepared a cadastral survey implementation strategy for Area 2, which includes launching a new bidding process to hire a firm to redo the survey in that area. There have been notable improvements in the other areas, as all contracts have been awarded for Areas 3 to 5, and a cooperation agreement has been signed with the Cadastral Institute of Lima (Instituto Catastral de Lima, ICL) for Area 6. The first and second stages of SICUN development have been completed, and stage 3 is in progress.

title.narrative: Relevant municipal staff trained and certified in management and use of the urban cadaster

comment.narrative: The National Urban Cadaster Specialization Program (PECUN 2025) has trained 1,900 participants, with strong performance in municipalities such as Villa El Salvador, Surquillo, and Los Olivos, demonstrating progress in technical capacity strengthening. Meanwhile, the Certification Program in Urban Cadastral Management is advancing in defining and validating competency standards and occupational profiles, laying the foundation for formal certification. Although results are not yet reflected in indicator figures, these actions establish the conditions for progressive compliance.

title.narrative: Municipalities with property value maps generated

comment.narrative: The indicator is in progress with an ongoing consultancy. Progress includes adjustments to homogeneous areas, methodological validation for estimating value per square meter, and technical coordination with MEF on machine learning models. Although final maps are not yet available, these actions consolidate the technical groundwork required to produce value maps that will enable municipalities to register approved valuations.

title.narrative: Number of people living in project municipalities with improved hazard exposure data

comment.narrative: The indicator remains unchanged as no approved Disaster Risk Prevention and Reduction Plans (Planes de Prevención y Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres, PPRRDs) incorporating urban cadastral information were reported by end-September 2025. However, progress includes three induction workshops (Lima, Chiclayo, Piura) with over 200 officials from 22 prioritized municipalities and 15 technical assistance meetings with six municipalities in Piura and Lambayeque to support integration of cadastral data. The first PPRRD with cadastral information was approved in October 2025 under an inter-institutional agreement with MVCS, COFOPRI, and the Municipality of Chiclayo. While not yet reflected in indicator figures, these actions establish the conditions for progressive compliance.

title.narrative: Methodology updated for improved urban cadastral data collection and maintenance

comment.narrative: As of December 2025, the PIU approved the Methodology for improved urban cadastral data collection and maintenance and prepared three Manuals: (i) Design of cadastral maintenance procedures, (ii) Urban cadastral survey, updating, and maintenance, and (iii) Cartographic standards applied to urban cadaster. The technical procedures and standards for collecting and preserving cadastral information were formulated by hiring individual consultants. Then, to measure this indicator as 100% completed, these Manuals must be approved and published. Therefore, this indicator is 67% achieved.

title.narrative: Communication strategy implemented to inform the target population about the cadastral survey process and its benefits

comment.narrative: The Communications Strategy was implemented in 13 districts corresponding to Areas 1 and 2. Area 1: Pimentel, Chiclayo, La Victoria, Piura, VeintisEis de Octubre, Catacaos, Castilla, Lambayeque, and JosE Leonardo Ortiz. Area 2: San Luis, Breña, Los Olivos, and Surquillo. As of December 2025, the communication campaigns for Areas 3, 4, 5, and 6 have begun. Following termination of the Area 2 contract, the communication strategy for this area will resume once a new contract is awarded.

title.narrative: Guidelines to ensure urban cadasters are linked to hazard data established

comment.narrative: The indicator is fully achieved through the preparation and delivery of guidelines that link the urban cadaster to disaster risk information. However, due to recent regulatory changes, updates to these guidelines and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) standards are underway in coordination with INDECI and CENEPRED.

title.narrative: Increase in the property tax base of project municipalities

comment.narrative: As of December 2025, 647,993 cadastral units have been surveyed across Areas 1 and 2, of which 113,852 units have successfully passed all quality control stages (from Area 1). The contract for Area 2 expired on May 12, 2025, and the service provider (Seresco) has not resolved persistent quality inconsistencies, which is leading toward contract termination. Consequently, the Implementing Agency has prepared a cadastral survey implementation strategy for Area 2, which includes launching a new bidding process to hire a firm to redo the survey in that area. There have been notable improvements in the other areas, as all contracts have been awarded for Areas 3 to 5, and a cooperation agreement has been signed with the Cadastral Institute of Lima (Instituto Catastral de Lima, ICL) for Area 6; (ii) The first and second stages of SICUN development have been completed.

title.narrative: Percentage of cadastral units updated by the project that register both men and women as property tax payers

comment.narrative:
661,924 (100% achieved) cadastral units have been surveyed (from Areas 1 and 2), of which 113,852 have passed the quality control stages. Cadastral surveying contracts for Areas 3 to 5 were awarded between April and August 2025. Area 6 is being implemented by ICL. The development of the SICUN phases and modules is as follows:
Phases I and II (100% achieved): - Cadastral Survey (Mobile App and SICUN Web) - Cadastral Maintenance (Cadastral Maintenance and TUPA Procedure) - Geographic Information System (Web Viewer and Thematic Reports)
Phase III - Cadastral Information (Geo Portal, Control Board, and Citizen Consultation) - Interoperability (LADM model and information from different institutions)

title.narrative: Percentage of grievances/complaints resolved in 20 working days

comment.narrative: From September 2023 to December 2025, citizens submitted 855 cases: queries (816), grievances (28), complaints (10), and denunciations (1) through the GM. The PIU has addressed 855 cases (out of the 855 received cases, 100% of which were resolved). Of these, 50% were filed by women and 50% by men, with an average resolution time of four days per case. The cases were entered through the following communication channels: GM website (95), toll-free line (579), email (20), GM System (138), and attention modules (23).

title.narrative: Adoption of updated property valuation methodology

comment.narrative: This indicator is 100% achieved and implemented in 2024. The following methodologies were approved: On October 30, 2022, through Ministerial Resolution No. 309-2022-VIVIENDA, the methodology called Simplified Table for fiscal purposes materialized by the inclusion of an Official Building Unit Values (VUOE) Table (simplified Table of three items), enabling Municipalities to calculate the valuation of property assets as well as the property tax. The MVCS approved the extension of the application of the methodology for tax purposes on October 27, 2023, through Ministerial Resolution No. 469-2023-VIVIENDA. Additionally, on March 13, 2023, the Government approved a simplified cadastral survey form that reduces the costs of urban data collection and cadastral information.
